title: fix(plugin-sharing,plugin-webhooks): by_object lists sort by object instead of grouping on its API name
body:
Part of #24701
Clause-②: no

This is half (a) of the card. `sys_sharing_rule.by_object` and `sys_webhook.by_object` stop heading each group with an object API name. Both views now sort by object instead of grouping on it, the same route PR #24698 took for `sys_record_share.by_object`. Half (b), the record share's heading, is measured and analysed only, with no edit, and the card stays open for its decision. #24701 remains open after this PR lands.

Responsibility: the sharing-rule and webhook list views' grouping (`plugin-sharing`, `plugin-webhooks`) | a served surface names the target object by its label, never by its API name (the #24375 route; no console-side mapping) | admins reading Setup → Sharing Rules and Setup → Webhooks.

Readings are against objectstack `d20bf9b09` (this branch's base) and objectui at the console pin `.objectui-sha` = `12dc7b47c3`, by `git show` and `git grep`. No browser reading: there is no console build in this container.

## Premise, measured

- **Both views grouped on `object_name`.** `sys-sharing-rule.object.ts` and `sys-webhook.object.ts` declared `grouping: { fields: [{ field: 'object_name', … }] }` on `by_object`. `object_name` is a `Field.text` with `widget: 'object-ref'` on both objects, so it stores an object API name.
- **The group header draws that value as stored text.** In objectui at the pin, `ObjectGrid`'s `groupValueFormatter` maps a select value to its option label and a boolean to Yes / No, and returns nothing for anything else. `useGroupedData` then uses the raw value as the header label, and `GroupRow` draws `group.label`. Server-side grouping hands back raw values too (`ListViewGroupHeaderRow`). So each group read `crm_account`, `showcase_announcement` and so on.
- **The cell already names the object by its label.** objectui#12613 (an ancestor of the pin) registers a read face for `widget: 'object-ref'` (`ObjectRefCellFace`): the object's icon and its translated label. The Object column's cells were labelled, and the header above them was not.

## Route: option (ii), sort instead of group

- **(i) Group on a column that carries the label: none exists.** Neither object has a field that stores the target object's label. The `object-ref` face labels a cell at render time, but the group header does not use cell faces. So any grouping key draws stored text.
- **(ii) Drop the grouping and keep the sort: chosen.** `sort: object_name asc, label asc` is unchanged, so one object's rows stay together. The Object column stays first, and its cell draws the object's icon and label.
- **(iii) Keep the grouping:** this leaves the card's defect in place.

Four axes:

- *Real business need.* The views answer "which rules or webhooks act on each object". The sort keeps that answer together, and the labelled Object cell names each object on every row. What this gives up is the collapsible header and its count. No nav entry opens these views: `nav_sharing_rules` and `nav_webhooks` open the object's first view (`active`).
- *Long-term soundness.* No new column, no mapping, and no console change. A grouping can come back once a label-bearing grouping key is served, or once the console's group header draws a widget-hinted field through its face (see Acceptance notes).
- *Making AI mistakes harder.* The new pins refuse a grouping on any field that stores an object API name: an `object-ref` field, or a pointer pair's `referenceVia` type half. The sharing pin covers every object `objects/index.ts` ships, so it also covers `sys_record_share` and `sys_share_link`.
- *Startup focus.* One key removed per view. No new gate.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-sharing-rule.object.ts` | `by_object` loses `grouping`; the sort and columns are unchanged |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/sys-webhook.object.ts` | `by_object` loses `grouping`; the sort and columns are unchanged |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-sharing-rule.by-object.test.ts` | new pin, 3 cases |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/sys-webhook.by-object.test.ts` | new pin, 3 cases |
| `.changeset/24701-by-object-group-headers.md` | `patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` and `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks` |

Not touched: `sys-record-share.object.ts`, `packages/spec/**`, and every stored column, index and query. Also not touched: the #15194 epic's files (`sharing-rule-service.ts`, `bootstrap-declared-sharing-rules.ts`, `sharing-plugin.ts`, `declared-webhooks.ts`, `webhook-provenance.ts`, `webhook-outbox-plugin.ts`).

## Pins

Each pin file has three cases:

- **Enumeration with a non-empty guard.** It first asserts which fields store an API name: `object_name` on each sharing object, and `object_name` on `sys_webhook`. So the refusal below cannot pass on an empty set.
- **The refusal.** No list view groups on such a field.
- **A control.** `by_object` still sorts first on `object_name asc` and still shows `object_name` as its first column. The sharing control also asserts that `object_name` keeps its `object-ref` widget, the cell face's trigger.

**Ablation.** Each leg ran once at `7fa022b59`, under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, with a shell `trap` restoring `HEAD` on EXIT, INT and TERM. The anchor was `pagination: { pageSize: 100 },` (1 hit in each file). The replacement put `grouping: { fields: [{ field: 'object_name', order: 'asc', collapsed: false }] }` back in front of it. The tests import the object files by relative source path, and `@objectstack/spec` was built, so no rebuild sits between a mutation and its run.

| Mutation | File | Landed | Red | Restored |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| put the `object_name` grouping back into `by_object` | `sys-sharing-rule.object.ts` | anchor 1 → 0, grouping 0 → 1, blob `5597d023128a` → `23c624a69766` | `no list view groups on a field that stores an object API name`: received `[ "sys_sharing_rule.by_object: object_name" ]` · `Tests 1 failed / 2 passed` | blob == HEAD `5597d023128a`, `git diff HEAD` empty |
| put the `object_name` grouping back into `by_object` | `sys-webhook.object.ts` | anchor 1 → 0, grouping 0 → 1, blob `1e3bf6397b97` → `a946ffa35dc7` | same case: received `[ "sys_webhook.by_object: object_name" ]` · `Tests 1 failed / 2 passed` | blob == HEAD `1e3bf6397b97`, `git diff HEAD` empty |

## Verification

All readings below are on head `7fa022b59`, the final commit. Exit codes were captured before any pipe. Builds and tests ran under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`.

- **Build.** The dependency closures (`--filter '@objectstack/plugin-sharing^...'` and `--filter '@objectstack/plugin-webhooks^...'`), then both packages: exit 0.
- **Tests.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing test`: exit 0, `Test Files 50 passed (50)`, `Tests 1172 passed (1172)` (1169 + the 3 new). `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-webhooks test`: exit 0, `Test Files 20 passed (20)`, `Tests 215 passed (215)`.
- **Typecheck.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-webhooks typecheck`: exit 0. `check:test-typecheck` holds both ledgers unchanged: sharing 2 files / 3 errors, webhooks 0 / 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists both new pin files, so the test layer compiles them. The sharing program's 3 errors are the ledgered ones, in `position-graph.test.ts` and `sharing-rule.test.ts`, none in the new file.
- **Derived gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, with no paths after the last commit, gave 67 commands. 65 exited 0 on the first pass. `pnpm check:i18n` first exited 3 (prerequisite not met: no CLI build). Its own prescribed turbo build was run, and the rerun exited 0: `check-i18n-bundles: OK (10 package(s) — all bundles in sync, no undeclared authoring keys)`.
- **NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`.** Reason: exit 3, prerequisite not met. It reads every package's `dist/` (54 packages unbuilt here), which needs a whole-workspace build. This diff changes no package entry, export or build config. CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs it.
- **`--ran` reconciliation.** `Run reconciliation — 67 derived, 66 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`, exit 0.
- **Declared to CI, not run locally:** `test:repo` (no repo-project test or derived list names this diff), `pnpm lint`, the type-check lanes, `Build Core` and the full `Test Core` shards.

## Half (b), measured only (no edit)

A record share's heading is `recipient_id` (`nameField`, since PR #24698), a `Field.text` with no widget and no reference.

- **What is stored.** Two call sites write `sys_record_share`, both in `SharingService.grant()` (`sharing-service.ts`, the update at :1550 and the insert at :1579). `grant()` refuses every `recipientType` except `user` (ADR-0111 D7). The rule evaluator calls it with `recipientType: 'user'` (`sharing-rule-service.ts:2177`), expanding team, business-unit and position recipients into one row per user. So every row written at `d20bf9b09` is a `user` grant, and its `recipient_id` is a `sys_user` id. The read gates match only `recipient_type: 'user'` (`sharing-service.ts` :589, :665, :877). The select still declares `user`, `group`, `position` and `unit_and_subordinates`, held equal to `RecordShareRecipientType` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts:104`). No writer produces the last three. No example app seeds the object.
- **Is there a recipient-type field?** Yes: `recipient_type`, a required select defaulting to `user`.
- **The console at the pin.**
  - The H1 is `recordDisplayValueAt(data, declaredNameField(…))` in `page:header` (`containers.tsx`). That is the stored text, so the H1 reads a raw user id. A field's widget face is not consulted.
  - With no widget, the Recipient column of `all_shares`, `granted_by_me`, `by_object`, `manual_grants` and `rule_grants` draws the same raw id.
  - `sys_sharing_rule.recipient_id` declares `widget: 'recipient-picker'`. Its face (`RecipientCellFace`, objectui#12613) names a `user` id by an exact-id `sys_user` read, keyed by the row's `recipient_type`. `group` is not a kind it knows, so a `group` row would draw as stored text.
- **How the console would label a pointer pair here.** `resolveRecordPointer` (`packages/fields/src/index.tsx:3291`) takes the `referenceVia` sibling's stored value as the object name. `recipient_type` stores `user`, not `sys_user`, so a pair on it would ask for an object called `user`. A declared pair needs a sibling column that stores an object name. Even then, the H1 draws the title field's stored id, and the Details tab hides the title field, so its pointer card would not draw.
- **ADR-0079.** `lookup` and `user` are title-ineligible types (`packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts`). A `formula` with a text result is eligible.

The options and the four-axis analysis are in the dev report on #24701. No edit was made to `sys-record-share.object.ts`.

## Acceptance notes

- **The console's group header does not use cell faces.** `groupValueFormatter` labels select and boolean values only, so a grouping on an `object-ref` or `recipient-picker` field heads its group with the stored value while the cells below are labelled. After this PR, no served objectstack view groups on such a field (the pins hold that), so nothing reaches it today. Carrier: none.
- **The record shares' Recipient column draws a raw user id** in five views, the list-side twin of half (b)'s heading. It is measured above and belongs to half (b)'s decision on #24701.
